previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypothyroidism, anxiety, and osteoporosis was admitted for abdominal heaviness concerning for an anginal equivalent. Evaluation revealed negative troponins, no EKG changes indicating ischemia, and a benign abdominal exam. The symptom resolved and was attributed to stress and possible gastritis from high-dose aspirin without PPI coverage. She was restarted on omeprazole and transitioned to 81 mg aspirin daily. Her anxiety, exacerbated by a verbally abusive husband and family stressors, was addressed with social work and continuation of doxepin, with a recommendation to consider an SSRI. Macrocytic anemia and thrombocytopenia were noted, with borderline low ferritin; she was discharged on thiamine and folic acid with a recommendation for outpatient hematology evaluation. She remained stable, with improved labs and no cardiac or respiratory complications, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old with pmhx of CAD s/p CABG and PCI, 
HTN, HL, and anxiety who presented with abd pain, n/v and chills 
subsequently developing hypotension, initially admitted to the 
ICU given pressor requirement.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
===================================
# Hypotension:  Patient developed hypotension in the ED after 
re-presenting with worsening abdominal pain, nausea and 
vomiting.  There was concern for new inferior ST elevations on 
her ECG, for which cardiology was consulted, and recommended 
serial enzymes and a TTE.  CTA showed no evidence of colitis, no 
vascular changes, no aneurysm, no diverticulitis.  She had an 
ECHO which showed hyperdynamic LV but no focal changes, trops 
negative so unlikely cardiogenic in nature. Her CTA A/P showed 
chronic L1 compression fracture with concern for mild 
retropulson and cord compression, for which spine was consulted 
and found a normal neurologic exam and chronic findings on 
imaging. Initially the ED plan had been overnight observation 
for ___ consultation, and she was treated with cefepime and 
vancomycin, however in observation she became hypotensive, with 
the lowest SBP in the ___, for which she received 2L NSS and 
subsequently a femoral CVL was placed (site at patient's 
request) and norepinephrine was started. She denied taking more 
than her prescribed dose of Metoprolol. With fluids and 
antibiotics she improved and was quickly transferred to the 
medicine floor where her Metoprolol was held.  TFTs were highly 
suggestive of sick euthyroid.  She remained normotensive and 
Metoprolol was ultimately re-introduced at a lower dose than her 
home medication which she tolerated well. 

# Likely Community Acquired Pneumonia:  Patient had persistent 
basilar crackles, left greater than right and abnormal CXR in 
setting of presentation with fever/hypotension/cough is 
concerning for a community acquired PNA.  It is possible that 
the broad spectrum antibiotics she was initiated on at 
presentation and the CTX she was continued on for UTI had 
partially treated a PNA.  She was started on a course of 
Levofloxacin for an additional 5 days to complete a total of a 7 
day antibiotoic course for pneumonia.  She was encouraged to use 
Incentive spirometer for likely component of atelectasis.  

# Anemia- Patient with a macrocytic anemia with a drop in hgb 
from 13.7 to 10 post fluids. No evidence of hemolysis with 
normal LDH, Fibrinogen, Haptoglobin. She had a normal B12 and 
folate.  RBC morphology was normal on two separate examinations. 
 There was no protein gap so less likely a paraproteinemia 
contributing. Ultimately her H/H uptrended and remained stable 
without any specific intervention.

# Thrombocytopenia: Patient with worsening thrombocytopenia to 
___ from prior baseline low 100s. 4T score was 2, so unlikely 
HIT. No evidence of DIC based on labs. Medication effect was 
considered, however besides antibiotics, there were no clear 
offending agents at this time.  Platelets subsequently improved 
with ongoing treatment of infection as above and were 108 at 
discharge. 

# Abdominal pain: Resolved quickly after admission.  This was 
still of unclear etiology given no clear evidence of UTI on UA, 
CTA A/P not explanatory of symptoms, LFTs unremarkable. Per 
discussion with radiology, there is some low density material in 
the uterus which was nonspecific and could represent endometrial 
thickening vs. fluid so a transvaginal ultrasound was performed 
and additionally found to be normal.  She was given Zofran and 
Ativan for subsequent episodes of nausea (which were not 
associated with emesis).  At time of discharge she was 
tolerating a regular diet, had moved her bowels and had no 
further abdominal pain. 

# ECG changes: Concern for inferior ST changes in ED, troponins 
negative. Seen by cardiology who recommended TTE.  She continued 
home ASA, and Rosuvastatin.  She had stable RBBB with LAFB and 
no further events this admission.  TTE showed mild symmetric 
left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved global biventricular 
systolic function.
